description:
pkix-ct/Cargo.toml, all public types

Non-negotiable #6 in AGENTS.md:

> They [public result/error types] SHOULD support `serde::Serialize +
> Deserialize` behind a `serde` feature flag for cross-process /
> persistent caches.

`pkix-ct` already has `serde` as an optional dep (gated on
`log-list-json` for the input JSON parsing). It does NOT expose
`Serialize/Deserialize` on its public types behind a `serde` feature
flag for caller use.

Public types that should support serde behind a feature:

- `Error` — for cross-process error reporting
- `SignedCertificateTimestamp` — for cache keys, audit logs, replay
- `SctList` — for the same
- `CtLog` and `CtLogList` — for caller-side trust store
  persistence
- `MerkleAuditPath` — for proof persistence (a caller cached a
  proof and wants to replay it)
- `SignedTreeHead` — for STH cache (extremely common: a TLS server
  caches the latest STH it has verified)

Today none of these derive Serialize/Deserialize. Caller wanting to
cache a parsed SCT has to:

- Re-parse from the wire bytes on every cache lookup (slow), OR
- Define their own caller-side mirror struct with serde + a
  conversion impl on both sides (boilerplate), OR
- Cache the SCT wire bytes and re-parse on hit (acceptable, but
  silly given the struct is already in memory).

Recommendation: add a `serde` feature:

```toml
[features]
serde = ["dep:serde", "der/serde", ...]
```

Derive `Serialize + Deserialize` on every public data type behind
`#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(...))]`. This is a one-line
change per type plus a feature in Cargo.toml.

Cost: ~10 derive lines, one new feature, zero runtime cost (only
compile-time and dep-graph cost for opted-in callers).

Benefit: cross-process caches, persistent STH stores, audit logs,
replay testing all become trivial.

Priority P1 because adding `Serialize/Deserialize` derives later is
technically non-breaking but the cache-key contract has implications
for which fields are present and what their types are; deciding
this BEFORE callers have built workarounds is a lot easier than
after.
title: No serde feature on cache-friendly result types — non-negotiable #6 says SHOULD support serde behind a feature flag
